[spoiler=
[pre]The Globalist[/pre]]

Yusuf and Faris Al-Mansoori were waiting outside the back entrance to the large meeting room of the parliaments building. Yusuf had already given a few speeches, during which Faris had stood next to him. Now, however, Faris was going to stand before a much smaller audience of people whose perceptions of him mattered. He grew nervous; the fact that he did not know what the topic of the day was did not help him.

Eventually, a government worker came and opened the door for them. Yusuf took the lead, stopping after a few paces to beckon his brother to follow. Faris obliged.

The stage was brighter than the other ones he had stood upon, the overhead lights beaming down on him almost as bright as the desert sun. Yusuf walked calmly to the podium that awaited him, looking over the audience. The parliament sat in wooden folding chairs, and the air conditioning blasted cool air far above them to provide some minor respite from the sweltering heat of the summers day. The audience clapped as the announcer introduced Yusuf and Faris, and when the applause quieted down, Yusuf began.

[i]Greetings, people of this great nation. Today, I will be speaking of international Hydronian affairs. There is much to cover, so while I would like to extend the introduction, it is imperative that we commence.[/i] He paused for a short while, looking over the room. [i]I am certain that you all understand the position that Hydronia is in globally. We are one of the powers of the world. Our industry is capable of overcoming the majority of Erenes and our military might has the potential to become a great unweatherable storm to our enemies. However, although our position is strong, this nation is, unfortunately, in decline.[/i]

[i]First, I turn to the international agreements that we have. These greatly disfavor Hydronia. Our citizens are being cheated by those whom we call our greatest allies. This has come about due to a series of errors by the previous presidencies, and I have every intend to set things right with other nations.[/i]

Faris nodded, proud of what his brother was saying. They had spoken about the problems that the common people of the nation faced and came to fix it, and Faris was glad that they were in a position to fix the issues.

[i]For this purpose, I will be attempting to cause a depolarization of the Shamat continents. It is in our best interest to work together with the international community as a whole instead of closing ourselves off. It is time to let go of past struggles, of past bitterness, and to move on to something new. We have the capability to move on. There are many business partners in the Western world with whom we could do business with; the influx of additional wealth would increase the quality of life all around. The undue stresses and labors imposed upon us by our allies will end soon, as Hydronia opens up to the international world![/i]

Some members of the parliament clapped wildly, and others merely sat there. The reaction was mixed. Although they had all appreciated the quality of Yusufs oration, not all were in agreement with him. However, it was abundantly clear that he was already starting to change the hearts of the parliament; if this same speech was given by the previous president, he would have been booed off the stage and promptly replaced by another one, effectively being barred from politics for the rest of their life.

Faris watched as, eventually, every member of the audience clapped. Some stood. He was in complete agreement with his brother up until his last point, and he felt a slight twinge of pain in his heart. His brother, whom he had previously agreed with, was speaking things that were against what the pair of them had originally thought.

------------------------------------

The pair of them walked off the stage at the conclusion of the meeting. The leader of parliament, Omar ibn Abdullah, had given a speech after them, which Faris, seated next to Yusuf upon the stage, did not pay attention to. Now, as they walked together through the backstage exit, there was a silence between them. Faris walked behind his brother through the narrow corridors of the backstage area. There was some discontent brewing in his heart, though he was convinced that he could try to talk his brother out of this path he was taking the nation.

Faris began when he and his brother finally left the backstage area. [i]Yusuf, what is your plan with what you were speaking on stage?[/i]

[i]What do you mean?[/i]

Faris paused. [i]Do you intend to remove Hydronia from our alliance, THEP?[/i]

After choosing his words carefully, Yusuf answered. [i]I believe we should reexamine our alliances and international relationships and pursue those that have the greatest potential to cause great benefit to our nation. The nations of the West, although-[/i]

[i]Yusuf, please,[/i] Faris interrupted, [i]you don't need to deliver a speech to me. Just answer the question.[/i]

The brothers stopped in the middle of the corridor. There was an unpleasant quiet in the air.

[i]Yes,[/i] he answered after a long pause, [i]its my intent to remove Hydronia from THEP.[/i]

[i]And ally ourselves with the decadent Western world?[/i]

[i]The West has opportunity for us. We have made a great error in separating ourselves from them. Our current allies are 

[i]Bullshit! You know thats bullshit![/i] Faris paused for a little moment, reigning back the volume of his voice. [i]Weve benefited greatly from our current alliances, and even if THEP needs some structural changes and to be more proactive, we should continue our alliances. Have you forgotten how many of our brothers have died in war against the West? Our own father[/i]

[i]...I have not forgotten, no, but what do you want to be done? Do you want to annihilate the West and be destroyed in return? Shall we keep up this cold war between ourselves and them? We, alone, are outmatched, and our allies can be detrimental at times. For each benefit that they bring, they bring their own share of geopolitical issues.[/i]

Faris could not find the words to continue his argument. For a few seconds, they stood there. Eventually, he spoke.

[i]Are we really to abandon the alliance that has been faithful to us, and us to them?[/i]

[i]I am president of Hydronia, not president of THEP. I am faithful only to the people of this nation, not an international alliance. I will serve an international alliance should it provide benefits to our nation, but otherwise, I see it as a detriment.[/i]

[i]But-[/i]

[i]I think thats quite enough. We can speak of this later, but I am cemented in this position. Nothing can change it. Right now, I have more urgent matters to attend to.[/i]

Yusuf nodded, turned, and left, leaving Faris standing in the corridor of the parliamentary building. In that moment, the discontent in his heart began to ferment into something else.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=
Defender of Hydronia
[pre]METAMORPHOSIS[/pre]]

Since his youth, Faris had always been considered somewhat erratic. He was difficult to read as a child, and growing older had only tamed this body, but the inner flames of his afflicted soul still burned brightly beneath the surface. Some especially perceptive people could see the truth behind his eyes, but no one dared to say much to him of this.

Late at night, he walked through the halls of the presidential palace of Hydronia. He knew that his brother was most likely working late, as there was much paperwork for him to do. That was something that Faris always admired about his brother, the fact that he was diligent.

Faris opened the door to the presidents office. Immediately, Yusuf looked up from his desk and locked eyes with his brother.

[i]Faris, what ails you?[/i]

He stepped into the room. He thought of speaking to him to change his views, but Yusuf had already said that he would not change. The next step was to make him resign. But how could he ask his brother to resign from his post? He had no reason other than that he did not like the way Yusuf was planning to change the nation.

He moved closer, now standing on the other side of the desk. Yusuf grew slightly uncomfortable. [i]Would you like coffee? Tea?[/i]

[i]Some tea would be good, thank you.[/i]

Yusuf stood from his desk and moved to the back of the room to prepare it. [i]I was just speaking with the leader of the parliament about how to restructure some of the Hydronian government at the lower levels. He stepped out to use the restroom and will be back shortly.[/i]

[i]I will stay to greet him then.[/i]

Yusuf nodded, and turned his back to his brother to prepare the tea. In that moment, a deep, overwhelming hunger overtook Faris soul. He remembered vividly the dismissive tone of brother, and imagined in excessive detail the decline of the nation that would happen under his presidency. 

And in that moment, a fundamental change took place in his soul. There was the hunger, the wrath, but there was also something new. He had learned to keep his impulsive nature in check, but now the restraints were loosed to a point where they were no longer effective; a part of his psyche had died, and now that he knew that, he acted.

He quietly approached, unsheathed the jambiya from its scabbard in his belt, and plunged it into his brothers neck. There was a gurgle of blood, Yusuf reached behind himself in confusion. Faris stabbed him again, now on his side, piercing through his ribs. His brothers lungs filled with blood. In short order, Yusuf collapsed dead.

Faris stood over the corpse of his brother. His mind was not filled with primal emotions, but rather it raced, thinking and scheming. He had little time to do this before there were two knocks on the door, and it opened.

[i]Hello, Yusuf,[/i] an older voice spoke, [i]Ive returned. Now, let us resume-[/i]

Faris turned his head around. The man was none other than Omar ibn Abdullah, the leader of the parliament.

[i]Ah, its you, Faris. How are you? Have you seen your brother?[/i]

[i]Close the door, please.[/i]

Omar obliged, and began to approach. When he got close, he saw the fullness of the scene. Yusufs dead body behind the desk, the bloody knife, and the pool of blood on the floor.

Omar ibn Abdullah staggered back. [i]Youll be [b]shot[/b] for this![/i] he shouted.

Faris stepped closer, and with a quick motion, brought the knife to the mans throat. He pushed a little bit, cutting into the skin and causing some blood to drip.

[i]If you dont listen to me very carefully, it is [b]you[/b] who will be shot.[/i]

They locked eyes. Omar saw a wild, cunning animal in Faris gaze, and he grew fearful not only for his life, but for the nations future.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=
[pre]Ladies and Gentlemen, we present to you:      
  President of the Nation, Faris Al-Mansoori...[/pre]]

Faris, seated at the presidential desk, looks at the camera before him. The camera crew are much more efficient than last time. In minutes, the whole setup is assembled.

[i]Ready![/i] says the cameraman.

Faris nods, and quickly begins his speech.

[i][pre]People of Great Hydronia, I greet you all. It is with a heavy heart that I must announce to you that my dearest brother, Yusuf Al-Mansoori, has died. The details will be announced in an official statement later it was a horrific thing that I will not recount and will try to not remember. Please, forgive me, but I cannot subject myself to recall the details.

I, Faris Al-Mansoori, am your current president. Yusuf appointed me as his right hand man, and I, his brother, will continue the presidency as he would have wanted. I am familiarized deeply with his beliefs, and saw as they evolved throughout the years, with this final transformation in beliefs so serene being what caused his murder.[/pre][/i]

He took a moment, looking down at the desk. His tongue moved on its own.

[i][pre]I will uncover the secrets to the murder of Yusuf. That much, I say. And the murderer he will rot in the afterlife for all eternity![/pre][/i]

[i][pre]Now, there is much I have to take charge of. I apologize for the short message, I regret not writing more; however, I did need to say this now, or else I would have not been able to say anything at all.[/pre][/i]

As the camera clicked off, his countenance changed. From a sympathetic, grieving young man, he became a man filled with hate. He shot a glare into the corner of the room, where Omar ibn Abdullah stood. Behind the camera were twenty armed guards, each tasked with watching Omar to ensure his silence during the broadcast. Now that it had concluded, Omar spoke.

[i]Faris please, reconsider![/i]

He remained silent.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=
The Great Horseman]

The room is silent. A string of tension is taut among the audience.

Faris Al-Mansoori sits at a desk with a microphone pointed at his face. Hundreds of people sit in the chairs before him, and millions watch through the cameras. The new president leans back, piercing the audience with a gaze cold.

When he speaks, his voice is the sole sound audible to them.

[i]In the name of Allah, the most gracious and merciful, I speak to you now, great people of Hydronia.[/i]

[i]Yesterday, my dearest brother, Yusuf, was killed by a traitorous plot formed by the followers of [b]Shaytan[/b]. This great tragedy was orchestrated by a group of people, the members of which are in this very room.[/i]

Whispers spread. Silence returns when Faris speaks. [i]I welcome Omar ibn Abdullah to speak on this matter.[/i]

No one claps as the leader of Parliament steps onto the stage. He walks towards a podium prepared on the stage, with a guard holding a rifle shadowing him. As he arrives, he picks up the sheet of paper on the podium: a speech.

Omar pauses. [i]At approximately three in the afternoon yesterday when Yusuf was killed by this plot I was caught speaking of the murder. I had not yet known that it had taken place, but it would have been impossible for me to have known. For this reason I stand before you today.[/i]

[i]Before, I saw that there was no greater thing for the people of Hydronia to bow their heads to the West and live as a humble people this is why I had voted for Yusuf to become president. However, it seemed that he was changing his mind, and desired for Hydronia to be proud once more, and for this reason, I and my coconspirators arranged for his assassination.

In exchange for my life I[/i] He looks at Faris, pleading; the president glares back. [i]...I, like a snake, gave up the names of those who took part.[/i]

Faris waves his hand at Omar, and the guard next to him takes him by the arm and pulls him off the stage. The audience now has fear; they want to leave.

The president leans forward and picks up a piece of paper. [i]When I read your name, get out.[/i]

He clears his throat.

[i]Shaquille Iqbal

Mahdi Ally

Arif Farran

Berkant Saltik

Aysin Aga

Alabas Kurt

Ceyhun Kubilay

Binay Basar

Batihan Aksu

Akmanalp Poyraz

Idil Yalaz

Cetin Birol

Fahir Mutlu

Seda Caner

Borahan Odabasi

Dilmen Tanyu[/i]

Each name read, another person stands. Some are confused, others are angry, but to those that try to defy his orders, guards quickly come to force them out. To all, guards escort them out through the double doors at the far end of the auditorium. 

After a grueling portion of time had passed in the heat, President Faris stands from his chair, picking up the microphone. [i]That is all of the traitors that have been uncovered. I doubt that this plot will reemerge once more, not with this substantial amount of loss.[/i]

The parliament members breathe a sigh of relief, but the immediate danger is quickly replaced with a sense of overwhelming dread.

[i]Soon I say, soon I will bring Hydronia to new heights. We will move forward from this, as one; remember, it is the West that has done this to us. It is the West who killed our president, acting through the easily deceived. For this reason, you must follow the sound of my voice, or else the Western siren will draw you away. There is no peace where there cannot be coexistence. There is no coexistence when we cannot be allowed to have our politics undisturbed by the desires of foreigners![/i]

The audience, confused, start to clap, but Faris leaves quickly, leaving them wondering what would happen next.

[/spoiler]
